ing: cut up; or 1.5 lb bone-in chicken if bat is unavailable
st: Rinse the meat well and cut it into serving pieces. Wild game must be cooked completely, so plan for a long simmer.
Put the meat in a pot with [[3 cups]] water, the ginger, onion and garlic. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the meat is very tender and well past 165°F (74°C) inside.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the salt and pepper.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes, uncovered. Do not boil hard or the coconut milk may split.
Taste and adjust the salt. Remove the ginger slices if you like.
Ladle into bowls with broth and meat, and top with green onion.
Peel and coarsely grate the sweet potatoes into a large bowl. Chop the shrimp into small pieces.
Add the shrimp, green onion, flour, cornstarch, paprika, salt and pepper to the bowl.
Stir in the water to make a thick batter that holds together when scooped.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C). Check the temperature with a thermometer.
Drop in heaping tablespoons of batter, flattening slightly, and fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Lift the fritters out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Fry in small batches.
Serve warm with soy sauce or sweet chili sauce for dipping.
Wear gloves to peel the taro, since raw taro can irritate skin. Cut it into 1-inch chunks.
Put the taro in a pot with [[1.5 cups]] water and the salt and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the taro is fork-tender. Taro must be fully cooked.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the sugar.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring carefully, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the taro.
Stir in the vanilla if using, taste, and add more sugar if you like it sweeter.
Serve warm in bowls as a side dish or dessert.

ing: about 2 lb, or use 2 lb king crab legs
st: Bring [[4 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a large pot fitted with a steamer rack.
Place the crab on the rack, cover tightly, and steam for 25 to 30 minutes until the shell is bright orange-red and the meat is opaque.
Meanwhile combine the coconut milk, garlic and ginger in a small pan and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Use a heavy knife or nutcracker to crack the shell and claws, and be careful of the sharp edges.
Pull out the meat and put it in the warm coconut sauce.
Warm everything together for 3 minutes. Do not boil.
Serve with melted butter, lemon wedges and green onion.

ing: such as snapper, scaled and gutted
st: Rinse the fish and pat dry. Cut three diagonal slashes into each side so the marinade gets in.
Mix the lemon juice, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, pepper and [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Rub the mixture over the fish and inside the cavity. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and brush the grates with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil so the fish does not stick.
Grill the fish for 6 to 7 minutes per side without moving it, until the skin is charred and the flesh flakes at 145°F (63°C).
Move the fish to a platter and let it rest for 3 minutes.
Top with green onion and lemon wedges and serve with rice.
